capability: Provide one Windows command that downloads one exact immutable GitHub Release ZIP and safely adds it to an operator-selected update source through the existing Catalog publisher
searchEvidence: release.yml already creates a single-version update-source handoff by copying the canonical ZIP, rendering releaseNotes from CHANGELOG, and invoking scripts/create_update_catalog.py; the manual wrapper reuses this orchestration shape rather than adding Catalog serialization.

scripts/create_update_catalog.py is the sole locked atomic aggregate Catalog publisher and verifies every retained ZIP, inner release manifest, stable metadata, package hash, releaseNotes, and controlled write. Catalog v2 extends that same CLI with --catalog-schema-version and complete repeatable --notification-policy assignments.

scripts/edit_update_source_registry.py is the sole Windows ACL-preserving live Registry publisher. It already owns expected-revision, complete route plans, Catalog schema/digest, dry-run, lock, atomic replacement, repair, and rollback behavior; this wrapper never calls it or edits Registry JSON, and README links the separate complete-route R3 flow.

scripts/publish-github.ps1 owns repository creation and main/tag push while the protected release workflow owns tag/Release creation and immutable assets. Manual update-source deployment consumes an already published stable Release and must not duplicate or bypass either publisher.

Repository-wide reuse search found no existing PowerShell update-source deployment or path-custody helper. WindowsStablePathCustody is an internal product-runtime adapter, not a callable release-script contract; exposing or duplicating its full product API would widen architecture and packaging scope, so the wrapper implements only the minimum two directory custody handles plus one stable package read handle needed around its own destination paths and bytes.

GitHub Release metadata supplies the exact stable tag, draft/prerelease status, canonical ZIP name/size/SHA-256 digest, and the protected workflow-validated Release notes projection. The wrapper consumes the exact returned body without claiming byte equivalence to the pre-upload notes file. GitHub Release publishedAt is not the protected workflow's canonical published_at input, so the wrapper requires that canonical CatalogPublishedAtUtc as an explicit operator value instead of guessing or substituting metadata.

No existing script provides a one-command operator path from authenticated GitHub Release metadata to a retained multi-version local/UNC update source; the current 30-day Actions handoff is deliberately single-version and not ready to overwrite a production aggregate source.
semanticOwner: A thin Windows PowerShell orchestrator over authenticated GitHub Release metadata and the existing create_update_catalog.py aggregate publisher; live Registry routing remains exclusively owned by scripts/edit_update_source_registry.py and is outside this wrapper
terminalContract: scripts/deploy-update-source.ps1 is CmdletBinding SupportsShouldProcess and accepts a mandatory exact stable Version, mandatory CatalogPublishedAtUtc copied from the protected release workflow evidence or single-version handoff, an existing normalized absolute local-drive-or-UNC SourceRoot, CatalogSchemaVersion defaulted to 1, and repeatable VERSION=manual-only|notify NotificationPolicy assignments. The GitHub origin is pinned to Dennis40816/nvt_fw_combiner for v1.0.8 and is not operator-selectable. It requires gh and Python; authenticated gh release view must return tagName exactly v<Version>, draft false, prerelease false, a non-empty exact body, and exactly one canonical NvtFwCombiner-v<Version>-win-x64.zip asset with positive integral size and lowercase sha256:<64-hex> digest. It downloads only that ZIP into one GUID temporary root and rejects every metadata or downloaded-byte mismatch. GitHub Release publishedAt is never used as CatalogPublishedAtUtc. SourceRoot and its existing packages child must be ordinary directories on one normalized absolute local-drive-or-UNC chain; relative, provider-qualified, device, extended, ADS, wildcard, dot-segment, trailing-dot/space, missing, and every reparse-point/junction/symlink component from the drive/share boundary through SourceRoot/packages are rejected. All SourceRoot mutation, including custody files, ZIP admission, and Catalog replacement, occurs only inside one positive ShouldProcess decision; -WhatIf performs read/download/hash/full-chain validation and reports the plan without changing SourceRoot. After approval and immediately before any other durable write, the wrapper creates and opens invocation-owned custody files with CreateNew, DeleteOnClose, and non-delete-sharing handles directly beneath SourceRoot and packages; lack of filesystem support fails before staging or helper execution. It retains both handles across same-directory staging, no-overwrite admission, helper execution, and cleanup, rechecks the exact directory identities before releasing the handles, and lets handle close remove the custody files without path-based unlink. These handles prevent a parent rename/reparse swap and are path custody, not a second publication lock. The destination packages directory retains existing versions; an existing canonical ZIP is reused only when bytes match and a mismatch fails without overwrite. A new ZIP is copied to an invocation-owned same-directory GUID staging file and admitted through no-overwrite File.Move. After admission or exact existing-file match, the wrapper opens the canonical destination ZIP from its final path with a stable read handle that permits other readers but denies write/delete, revalidates exact file identity, size, and SHA-256 from that handle, and retains it until create_update_catalog.py completes; inability to acquire or stably revalidate package-byte custody fails before helper execution. Automatic cleanup is limited to a never-admitted unique staging file and delete-on-close custody files. Once no-overwrite admission succeeds, the final ZIP is never automatically deleted in any phase; a helper-preflight or later failure may leave a harmless unreferenced immutable orphan. README only tells the operator to retain and report that orphan: cleanup is outside this wrapper and forbidden until a repository-owned Catalog publisher operation proves under its existing lock that no v1/v2 Catalog references the exact path, version, or bytes. The wrapper writes the exact GitHub Release body to a temporary notes file and delegates every aggregate package/manifest/stable-metadata/releaseNotes/atomic-Catalog decision to create_update_catalog.py. CatalogSchemaVersion 1 is the default v1.0.7-to-v1.0.8 canary path and rejects every NotificationPolicy assignment; schema 2 passes every assignment through the existing helper and requires a complete exact assignment for every retained aggregate version, including explicit operator assignments for pre-existing versions rather than guessing. This makes v1.0.9 and later changelogs flow from their exact Release body without a hard-coded version branch. The script never creates a tag, GitHub Release, package, Catalog serializer, Registry serializer, or second Catalog lock/rollback owner, and it never reads or changes a live Registry; an optional Registry route remains a separate explicit invocation of scripts/edit_update_source_registry.py with its complete latest/available/deprecated plan and R3 approval. README replaces the old multi-step Catalog example with this canonical one-command path and retains one link to the separate Registry contract; docs/ci/release-package.md remains the lower-level audited package/handoff procedure owned by the existing release record. Download and notes temporary files are beneath one exact GUID root; transient SourceRoot artifacts are limited to the two delete-on-close custody files and a same-invocation staging file that is removed only if never admitted. Logs contain no token or release body, and fixed-D fake-gh/fake-python tests cover WhatIf, exact/wrong Release identity, metadata and downloaded-byte mismatches, existing exact/mismatching ZIPs, ambiguous helper failure, reparse/parent-identity drift, directory/package custody refusal, and complete v1/v2 notification-policy matrices without network, G-drive, GitHub, or live Registry mutation.

designReview.evidence: Independent R3 release/script design review confirmed P0-P3 = 0 and scoped Polytail PASS-WITH-HUMAN-GATE after incorporating the full findings batch. The wrapper is a thin Windows-only orchestrator pinned to Dennis40816/nvt_fw_combiner: it authenticates exact stable Release/tag/body/asset metadata, verifies downloaded size and GitHub SHA-256, requires the protected canonical CatalogPublishedAtUtc instead of substituting GitHub publishedAt, and delegates all aggregate v1/v2 Catalog serialization, stable metadata, releaseNotes, package/manifest verification, locking, and atomic replacement to the existing create_update_catalog.py owner. One ShouldProcess gate covers every SourceRoot mutation; WhatIf is read-only. Full-chain no-reparse validation, two non-delete-sharing DeleteOnClose directory-custody handles, and one stable final-package read handle bind parent and package identity/bytes through helper completion. Admission is no-overwrite, an admitted final ZIP is never automatically deleted after any failure, and automatic cleanup is limited to never-admitted staging plus handle-owned custody files. Catalog v1 remains the default canary, v2 requires complete explicit manual-only|notify assignments, GitHub Release body remains the version-neutral changelog source, and no Registry, GitHub publisher, serializer, lock, rollback owner, package builder, firmware semantic, memory range, mutation order, CRC/checksum behavior, or release payload is duplicated or changed. README becomes the single operator entry while the existing release-package and Registry authorities remain separate. Fixed-D fake-tool evidence is required for WhatIf, Release/digest/byte failures, idempotent exact reuse, mismatch/no-overwrite, ambiguous helper failure/orphan retention, reparse/identity/custody failures, and v1/v2 policy forwarding. Exact-head implementation review, canonical verifier, local/UNC canary, published-package evidence, and release-owner R3 attestation remain mandatory human/external gates.
